hypothesis: Jerome's email of 30 Sep 2026 (item 10) and the consolidated note (sections 18-20) ask to use the temperature sweep to study 'speciation': as the corruption falls the exact denoiser should commit to the sign of whole domains, more sharply at low temperature where domains are long (xi ~ exp(E_kink / Theta)), with Theta (physical temperature) kept apart from t (corruption level); and they state that the 1D field has no phase transition but a sharp crossover. None of this was measured: the audit of 9 Oct graded it NOT ADDRESSED. Two questions. (1) Commitment: when does the exact posterior decide the sign of a site, how does that depend on Theta and on the chain length relative to xi, and is it a second-order (covariance) effect -- the Gaussian twin with the same covariance commits at the same t -- or does the bimodality make the exact posterior commit earlier? The speciation time of Biroli, Bonnaire, de Bortoli and Mezard (2024), t_S = (1/2) ln Lambda with Lambda the largest covariance eigenvalue, is the natural scale. (2) Is the lattice chain the discretised gradient SPDE as far as its kinks are concerned: does its correlation length follow the continuum dilute-kink-gas law with the kink energy 2 sqrt(2)/3 as h -> 0?
design: Two parts, laptop, the TRUE kernel only (no learning). (a) commitment: per cell 2 reps x 2048 exact stationary chains (Phi4Chain.sample_batch), noised at 48 levels t geometrically spaced in [0.02, 4]; the exact posterior by grid BP at the registered grid (401 points on [-8, 8]) with the sign probability p_i = P(a_i > 0 | x_t) (bp_grid.grid_bp_batch(..., return_sign_prob=True), tested against brute-force enumeration); per level the commitment |2 p - 1| averaged over all sites and over the central sites (commitment.bulk_sites: 2 min(L/4, 8) sites), the share of signs guessed right, the posterior-mean MSE against the clean field (the MMSE), the mean posterior variance, the linear floor's MSE (LMMSE with the true covariance) on the same data, and the Gaussian twin's commitment and posterior variance in closed form (commitment.gaussian_twin: c_i = (2/pi) arcsin R_i, R_i^2 = 1 - v_i / Sigma_ii). Cells: E32's fixed-spacing axis (h = 1, L = 32, Theta in 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.5, 2); a length series at Theta = 0.2, h = 1 (xi = 19.5 sites) with L in 4, 8, 16, (32 from the axis), 64, 128, 256; and E32's other five cells (T0.5_iso_L32, T1_iso_L32, T2_iso_L32, T0.3_h0.5_L64, T0.3_h0.25_L128). The commitment time t_c is where the rep-pooled commitment curve first falls through 1/2 (commitment.crossing_time, linear in log t). (b) kink_energy: the transfer operator's correlation length (field.solve_spectrum, dense eigensolve, 2401 points on [-12, 12]) on Theta in 0.1, 0.125, ..., 0.3 (9 values) x h in 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32; the two finest spacings again on 4801 points (a check of the eigensolve's own discretisation, descriptive). Theory: for the continuum SPDE the transfer operator is exp(-h H), Theta H = -(Theta^2/2) d^2 + V, a double well with hbar = Theta, so xi_phys = Theta / (E_1 - E_0) with the tunnel splitting E_1 - E_0 ~ Theta^{1/2} exp(-S_0 / Theta), S_0 = int_{-1}^{1} sqrt(2 V) = 2 sqrt(2) / 3 = 0.9428 (the kink energy): ln xi_phys = S_0 / Theta + (1/2) ln Theta + c + O(Theta).

predeclared_predictions.P1: Calibration (an exactness check of the whole pipeline): on every cell of part (a), with the reps pooled, the share of signs guessed right equals (1 + commitment) / 2 (all sites) to within 0.01 on average over the 48 levels, and to within 0.05 at every level.
predeclared_predictions.P2: Fixed-spacing axis (h = 1, L = 32): the commitment time t_c (all sites) falls strictly as Theta rises, in all 7 consecutive pairs of the 8 temperatures.
predeclared_predictions.P3: The exact posterior commits EARLIER (larger t_c, all sites) than its Gaussian twin on the four fixed-spacing cells with Theta <= 0.5, and the excess t_c - t_c^twin is larger at Theta = 0.2 than at Theta = 2.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Length series at Theta = 0.2 (central sites): t_c rises with L across 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, each step by more than 0.02, and moves by less than 0.03 between L = 128 and L = 256.
predeclared_predictions.P5: Below the correlation length (L = 4, 8, 16, central sites): the least-squares slope of t_c against (1/2) ln(1 + Lambda_max(L)), Lambda_max the largest eigenvalue of the L x L covariance, lies in [0.8, 1.2].
predeclared_predictions.P6: Kink energy: at h = 1/16 and at h = 1/32 (2401-point eigensolve), the least-squares fit ln xi_phys = a / Theta + b ln Theta + c + d Theta over the nine temperatures 0.1-0.3 gives a within 2% of 2 sqrt(2) / 3 = 0.9428 (a in [0.924, 0.962]).
predeclared_predictions.P7: and the same fits give b in [0.35, 0.65] (the instanton prefactor's Theta^{1/2}).

predeclared_analysis: tools/make_extension_numbers.py read_e50_commitment (outputs/E50/commitment.csv: per cell the level-wise means over reps; t_c by commitment.crossing_time on commit_all, commit_bulk and twin_commit_all; a NaN crossing counts against every clause it touches) and read_e50_kink (outputs/E50/kink.csv, rows with n_fine = 2401; numpy least squares on [1/T, ln T, 1, T]). Descriptive, no prediction: the MMSE and the linear floor's MSE per cell and level (the note's section 24.5), the commitment curves themselves, the fit at coarser h (including h = 1, the operating lattice), the 4801-point check, and t_c against (1/2) ln(1 + Lambda_max) on every cell.

provenance_note: Written on 9 Oct 2026 before any E50 cell ran. Seen beforehand: E32's frozen fixed_h.csv correlation lengths at h = 1 for Theta = 0.2-2 (19.47, 6.08, 3.66, 2.75, 1.98, 1.53, 1.21, 1.06 sites), and, computed as INPUTS for choosing the length series, the largest eigenvalue of the L x L covariance at Theta = 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 2 for L = 4-256 (e.g. Theta = 0.2: 3.66, 6.80, 11.98, 19.25, 27.06, 32.89, 35.84). No commitment, sign probability or MSE was computed on any cell, and no spectrum below Theta = 0.2 or at h < 1 on the kink ladder. The bounds of P3 and P5 were set from two pencil calculations, not from data: a +-1 variable is committed to more than a Gaussian one at equal signal-to-noise (scalar, unit signal-to-noise: E|2p-1| = E|tanh y| = 0.68 for a = +-1 against (2/pi) arcsin(1/sqrt 2) = 0.50 for a ~ N(0, 1), checked by Monte Carlo on 2e6 draws), and for a Lorentzian spectrum the twin's posterior variance halves at gamma S(0) = 3, i.e. t = (1/2) ln(1 + S(0)/3), whose slope against (1/2) ln(1 + S(0)) over S(0) = 4-12 is about 0.9-1.05. The new code (bp_grid return_sign_prob, markov_score/commitment.py) is tested in tests/test_commitment.py; the BP regression tests pass (97 passed, 25 skipped).

outcome.P3: CONFIRMED. The exact posterior commits at higher noise than its Gaussian twin on every fixed-spacing cell, not only at Theta <= 0.5: t_c - t_c^twin = +0.466, +0.320, +0.227, +0.169, +0.118, +0.086, +0.072, +0.066 at Theta = 0.2 ... 2 (largest when coldest, as predicted).
outcome.P4: CONFIRMED. Theta = 0.2, central sites: t_c = 1.025, 1.302, 1.526, 1.679, 1.724 at L = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 (each step > 0.02), then 1.750 at 128 and 1.754 at 256 (+0.004 < 0.03): commitment time grows with the chain until the chain is several correlation lengths long, then saturates.

outcome.unregistered: Kink part. (i) The continuum limit is converged: xi_phys changes by 0.03% between h = 1/16 and 1/32 at Theta = 0.1 (1169.03 against 1168.69), and the 4801-point eigensolve agrees with the 2401-point one to 2e-12 in ln xi; the operating lattice h = 1 overestimates the continuum xi_phys by 4% (Theta = 0.1) to 9% (Theta = 0.3). (ii) Why the fit fails, as a reading and not a verdict: the local slope d ln xi_phys / d(1/Theta) between consecutive temperatures rises from 0.644 (Theta ~ 0.29) to 0.868 (Theta ~ 0.11); its deviation from the instanton form 2 sqrt(2)/3 - Theta/2 is -0.155 at Theta ~ 0.29 and -0.019 at 0.11, shrinking roughly like Theta^2 (deviation / Theta^2 between -1.5 and -2.2). That is consistent with the continuum dilute-kink law plus large next-order corrections at these temperatures, which a free four-parameter fit on Theta in [0.1, 0.3] trades off between a and b (collinear regressors). With b fixed at 1/2 and no correction term the fit gives a = 0.885. Settling the asymptotic constants needs Theta < 0.1 (xi_phys > 1000), not run. Commitment part. The exact t_c tracks (1/2) ln(1 + Lambda_max) within about 0.25 on every cell (descriptive); the twin commits later in the reverse process everywhere, so the bimodality, not only the covariance, sets when the denoiser commits: at Theta = 0.2, L = 32 the exact posterior is half-committed at t = 1.61 (noise variance 24 times the signal's), its Gaussian twin only at t = 1.15 (8.9 times).
